title: Customer choice microflow — incident evidence & short decision brief
summary: Compact, customer-facing draft that explains the recent inference integrity event, presents customer choices (opt-in replay, safe-mode), and bundles an evidence checklist + verification steps. Intended for quick status page entry + optional tenant-targeted message.
content:
Purpose and audience
This doc is a compact, customer-facing draft (shortform) for tenants affected by the inference-output integrity event that began 2028-02-14 07:12 UTC. Primary audience: engineering leads and platform owners at affected tenants. Secondary: product managers and legal/compliance contacts who will need evidence for audit.

TL;DR (for status page and quick emails)
- What happened: Intermittent output duplication and partial truncation for text-generation endpoints routed through our EU routing tier during 07:12–08:40 UTC. Root cause: a rare cache-eviction race during a transient autoscaling event combined with a model shard mismatch on fallback paths.
- Impact: ~2.4% of requests for affected tenants had either repeated tokens or early truncation; no customer data exfiltration detected; API auth unaffected.
- Current status: Mitigation deployed 08:50 UTC (cache replay protection + conservative shard routing). Service is back to normal; we are offering an opt-in replay and a lightweight verification evidence packet to tenants.

What customers need to know (concise bullets for status page)
- Time window: 2028-02-14 07:12–08:40 UTC (all times UTC).
- Symptoms: duplicated phrases in generated text, occasional premature end-of-stream.
- Affected endpoints: text generation (v1/complete, v1/chat) when routed via EU-inference tier; embeddings and non-text endpoints unaffected.
- Customer action: no mandatory action required. For tenants who prefer to reconcile outputs, we offer an opt-in replay plus an evidence package to help verify integrity.
- Safety: No compromised credentials; logs were read-only for retention and audit.

Evidence packet (what we will provide if tenant requests it)
- Timestamped operator timeline (UTC) covering autoscale event, cache evictions, fallback routing decisions.
- Sampled request/response pairs (redacted PII) for up to 24 hours for tenant verification.
- Hash manifest of model shards deployed during the window and fallback chain ids.
- Operator checksums and short trace ids to cross-link tenant-side logs.
- Reproduction notes: minimal repro harness used in staging and the mitigations attempted.

Opt-in replay offer (customer choice microflow)
We propose a simple opt-in flow for tenants who want our assistance replaying requests to generate replacement outputs. Options:
- Full replay (operator-assisted): Redwood will re-run the recorded inputs in an isolated, deterministic environment pinned to the pre-event model shard and provide the resulting outputs. Recommended for customers with high-integrity requirements.
- Sampling replay (self-serve): Tenant gets a curated sample (<=500 requests) with reproduced outputs and a short comparison report. Good for spot-check verification.
- Decline: No action; service is already restored and most customers will not need a replay.

Replay constraints and notes
- Replays are best-effort and determinism is influenced by model stochasticity and temperature parameters; we will fix seeds and pin to the same quantization/profile to maximize fidelity.
- We will not charge for operator-assisted replays for customers affected above a 1% error threshold during the window.
- Replays may take up to 72 hours to schedule for large tenants; sampling replays are typically <24 hours.
- If tenant wants replayed outputs to replace live records, we provide a verification checklist and optional signed attestation of process.

Suggested verification checklist for tenants (step-by-step)
1) Confirm you have a list of request timestamps and request ids from your side for the window (we provide trace ids).
2) Approve a data-redaction plan (we can redact PII before replaying).
3) Select either Full or Sampling replay option.
4) Receive evidence packet + replay outputs.
5) Compare outputs using provided diff script (we include a small comparator and suggested acceptance thresholds).

Draft status page copy (short)
Title: Partial duplication and truncation — EU inference tier (mitigated)\Body: We experienced intermittent duplication and early truncation for some text-generation requests in the EU inference tier between 2028-02-14 07:12 and 08:40 UTC. We deployed a mitigation at 08:50 UTC that prevented further occurrences. Customers experiencing anomalies can request a free, operator-assisted replay or a sampling verification pack. No credential compromise detected. Further details and evidence-request instructions are available via your account rep or the link included in this message.

Draft targeted customer note (email/snippet for affected tenants)
Subject options: "Redwood — short incident recap and replay offer" / "Follow-up: EU inference tier anomaly and replay offer"\Hi <customer-first-name>,\On 2028-02-14 we observed an issue affecting a small portion of text-generation traffic routed through our EU tier which resulted in duplicated tokens or truncated responses for some requests. We resolved the root trigger and rolled mitigations at 08:50 UTC.\If you’d like us to re-run requests from the affected window and provide replacement outputs, please reply with your preferred option (Full replay / Sampling) and confirm a redaction policy. We will prioritize customers by impact level.\Regards,\Maya on behalf of Redwood Customer Operations

Internal operator notes (short, for CS + SRE coordination)\- Root cause summary: race condition between cache-eviction callback and fallback shard assignment on autoscale; a small set of in-flight requests read a partially-reset KV cache leading to duplicate token emission path.\- Permanent fix path: add a short quiesce window during autoscale + strengthening fallback shard guarding; follow-up PR: SERVE-ops-342.\- Immediate mitigations we applied: conservative shard routing, cache replay protection patch, tightened autoscale cooldown to 45s.\- Monitoring changes suggested: add a duplication-rate alert (threshold 0.5% over 10m) and surface sample diffs in the per-tenant console.

Operator checklist before sending customer notes\- Confirm tenant impact list (ops will produce list by 09:30 UTC).\- Prepare redacted sample bundle for each tenant opting in.\- Confirm scheduling window for operator-assisted replay.\- Legal to sign off on attestation templates if customer requests formal certificate.

Open questions / notes to self\- Do we want to expose a self-serve "request replay" button in the tenant console for future events? (Pros: faster; Cons: potential resource spikes).\- Decide SLA language for replays (we draft a short-term exception that replays are best-effort).\- Check whether we should proactively notify EU-only partners that use dedicated capacity (they may have different expectations around replays).

Suggested next steps (owner: Maya / CS lead)
1) Finalize the short status page text and post update (by 10:00 UTC).
2) Ops to produce per-tenant impact CSV and initial sample bundles (by 11:00 UTC).
3) Legal to review attestation template and replay consent text (by EOD).
4) CS to send targeted tenant emails with opt-in instructions and scheduling link (CS to triage high-impact customers first).

Appendix: quick timeline (UTC)
- 07:12 — first alerts: increased duplication rate in EU tier metrics.
- 07:18 — initial mitigation: disabled one autoscale policy (temporary).- 07:34 — SRE root-cause debug, identified cache->fallback race hypothesis.
- 08:05 — rollback attempt of fallback code (did not fully prevent duplicates).
- 08:40 — full mitigation plan compiled; final patch staged.
- 08:50 — mitigation deployed (cache replay protection + conservative shard routing).
- 09:10 — metrics confirm duplication rate returned to baseline.

Draft sign-off block (for quick approvals)\- CS lead: [ ]\- SRE lead: [ ]\- Legal: [ ]\- Product: [ ]

Notes on tone and phrasing: keep customer-facing text short, avoid internal jargon (replace "shard" with "model instance" in external copy unless customer is technical), offer choices and attach an evidence kit.

End of draft.

(Internal: store final evidence bundles at the per-tenant folder: drive link to be populated post-signoff.)
